info.name: cascivo
info.summary: Add, update and audit cascivo components in your project
info.description:
The cascivo CLI. Components are copied into your project as source you own (the shadcn model); the CLI resolves their dependencies, installs the runtime packages they need, and checks your code against the cascivo contract.

Run it without installing: `npx cascivo <command>`.

1.meaning: the command failed or was used wrongly

options.name: --help
options.summary: Show this help, or a command's help

commands.name: create
commands.summary: Scaffold a new ready-to-run app (shell + nav + theme)
commands.description: Scaffold a new app pre-wired with the cascivo app shell, side navigation, header and a theme. Writes a new directory; it does not install dependencies.

arguments.name: name
arguments.summary: Directory and package name of the new app

options.name: --framework
options.description: `cloudflare` is a client app and its API, deployed as one Cloudflare Worker.

options.name: --example
options.summary: Add a Worker-backed example page (cloudflare only)
options.description: board (multiplayer page on a Durable Object), agent (AI assistant that answers with UI; needs --runtime react), notes (local-first, offline edits), import (CSV import on a Workflow), files (uploads into R2), export (PDF/PNG via Browser Run), usage (Workers Analytics Engine charts), crud (a D1 table behind DataTable's server mode), live (ops dashboard fed by a Queue), voice (Workers AI speech in and out), publish (views published as pages in D1), webhooks (signed GitHub deliveries), digest (weekly PDF email on a Cron Trigger), search (Vectorize + Workers AI), checkout (Stripe Checkout), newsletter (double opt-in via Amazon SES), social (post to Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn, Threads and Buffer; needs --auth).

options.name: --auth
options.summary: Guard the Worker: access, email, oauth, or email,oauth (cloudflare only)
options.description: `access` refuses every request Cloudflare Access did not let through. `email` adds accounts with emailed sign-in links; `oauth` adds GitHub, Google and LinkedIn sign-in. With either, every API write needs a signed-in user. `email,oauth` enables both.

options.name: --template
options.summary: Start from a marketplace template (@ns/name or owner/repo/name)

options.name: --from
options.description: A blueprint names the app, its framework, theme, runtime, examples and auth, and its pages as [{ "title", "block"? }]: each page renders that registry block, wired into the routes and the side nav. It replaces the other options; the blueprint is copied into the app as cascivo.app.json.

options.name: --sections
options.summary: Comma-separated nav section labels (one component each)

options.name: --package-manager
options.summary: Package manager named in the README and next steps

examples.run: npx cascivo create my-app --framework cloudflare --example crud --yes

commands.name: init
commands.summary: Set up cascivo in the current project
commands.description: Writes cascivo.config.ts and installs the runtime dependencies (@cascivo/core, @cascivo/tokens, @cascivo/themes and the @preact/signals-react peer), plus cascivo as a dev dependency for the config's types.

options.name: --no-install
options.summary: Write files only; print the install commands to run yourself

options.name: --yes
options.summary: Accept defaults, never prompt (implied when stdin is not a TTY)

commands.name: add
commands.summary: Add components or a template to your project
commands.description: Copies component source (TSX + CSS module) from the registry into your project, resolving component dependencies, and installs the npm packages they need. Also installs templates (@ns/name) and third-party components (owner/repo/name).

options.name: --dry-run
options.summary: Show what would be written without writing

options.name: --no-install
options.summary: Don't install npm-distributed entries or deps; print the commands instead

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List components available in the configured registry

options.name: --installed
options.summary: Only list components already installed in this project

commands.name: update
commands.summary: Update installed components to the current registry version
commands.description: Without a component argument, updates everything in the lockfile.

commands.name: search
commands.summary: Search components across the configured registries

options.name: --registry
options.summary: Restrict the search to one registry namespace

commands.name: view
commands.summary: Preview a component or template before installing
commands.description: Prints its files, dependencies and description without writing anything.

commands.name: theme
commands.summary: Install a first-party theme, or build a custom one

commands.name: add
commands.summary: Install @cascivo/themes and print the import + data-theme wiring

arguments.name: name
arguments.summary: light, dark, warm, flat, minimal, midnight, pastel, brutalist, corporate, terminal, cyberpunk or arcade

commands.name: create
commands.summary: Turn a theme-builder config into an owned <name>.theme.css

commands.name: eject
commands.summary: Eject specific tokens into a scoped local override file
commands.description: Restyle a component without forking it.

arguments.name: component
arguments.summary: The component whose tokens to eject

options.name: --scope
options.summary: CSS selector the overrides are scoped to

options.name: --dry-run
options.summary: Print the override file without writing

commands.name: generate
commands.summary: Generate TSX from a ViewConfig JSON file
commands.description: The ViewConfig is what the MCP scaffold_view tool produces. With --out, the written file is formatted with the project's formatter when one is found.

options.name: --from
options.summary: Import every component from one package instead of the components directory

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check components for rule violations
commands.description: Checks components for cascivo rule violations (banned React hooks, hardcoded strings, missing @cascivo/react exports). In an adopter project it also verifies the runtime dependencies copied source needs are declared in package.json, and compares installed components against the registry (copy-paste drift).

options.name: --ci
options.summary: Exit non-zero when violations or missing runtime deps are found

options.name: --drift
options.summary: Only compare installed components against the registry (copy-paste drift)

commands.name: audit
commands.summary: Audit AI-generated code against the cascivo contract
commands.description: Finds hard-coded values that should be tokens, invented props, missing required props, and raw strings where i18n is expected.

options.name: --fix
options.summary: Rewrite unambiguous CSS literals to their token equivalents

options.name: --contract
options.summary: Use this audit-contract.json instead of the bundled one

options.name: --verbose
options.summary: Report which contract source was used

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Configure the cascivo MCP server

commands.name: init
commands.summary: Add the cascivo MCP server to your agent's project config
commands.description: Adds `npx -y @cascivo/mcp`. Other servers in the file are kept; an existing cascivo entry is left as it is.

options.name: --client
options.summary: Which agent config to write: claude (.mcp.json), cursor (.cursor/mcp.json) or vscode (.vscode/mcp.json)

options.name: --dry-run
options.summary: Print the file instead of writing it

commands.name: app
commands.summary: Change an app made from a blueprint

commands.name: add
commands.summary: Add to the app

commands.name: page
commands.summary: Add a page, optionally rendering a registry block
commands.description: Appends the page to cascivo.app.json and writes the page, its block and the route and nav entries. Files edited since they were generated are merged three ways; a clash is left with conflict markers and the command exits non-zero.

options.name: --block
options.summary: The registry block the page renders

examples.run: npx cascivo app add page "Users" --block users-table-page

commands.name: registry
commands.summary: Build a static registry

commands.name: build
commands.summary: Build registry.json and file payloads from a registry manifest
commands.description: The output is ready to host on any static file server.

examples.run: npx cascivo registry build --in cascivo-registry.json --out public/r

commands.name: template
commands.summary: Author marketplace templates

commands.name: init
commands.summary: Scaffold a new template (source + manifest + registry entry)

options.name: --repo
options.summary: Repository the template will be hosted in

examples.run: npx cascivo template init sales-dashboard --category dashboard --components card,line-chart

commands.name: tokens
commands.summary: Design-token interchange

commands.name: import
commands.summary: Import external design tokens as cascivo overrides (not yet implemented)
commands.description: Reserved for importing W3C design-tokens JSON. This release prints a notice and changes nothing.

commands.name: email
commands.summary: Email tooling

commands.name: lint
commands.summary: Check rendered email HTML for client support and dead links
commands.description: The same conformance lint @cascivo/email exposes as `lint()`. It lints rendered HTML, not templates. The matrix is fetched from https://www.caniemail.com/api/data.json and cached in the temp directory for a day. Links that go nowhere (`checkLinks()`: empty, `#`, relative, an unreplaced merge tag, or a placeholder domain such as example.com) fail it too. A caveat (partial support, a localhost or http: link) never fails the command.

options.name: --data
options.summary: Use a local copy of the matrix instead of fetching

options.name: --refresh
options.summary: Re-fetch the matrix even if the cache is fresh

options.name: --check-links
options.summary: Also request every http(s) URL; one answering 4xx/5xx, or not at all within 10s, fails the command

1.meaning: a floor client cannot support something, a link cannot work, or the command failed

examples.run: node render.js | npx cascivo email lint -
